observations: All 22 reference-management captures show legible discovery, pending-download, local-import, binding and relocation layouts; fixed controls remain within the captured windows without overlap.
Reference detail and review areas intentionally scroll; partially visible final text lines at viewport edges are not fixed-control clipping.

All 18 scroll reference panels show coherent top/notch/bottom text and control layouts; long path edit boxes show bounded horizontal views and content crosses panel edges as expected during scrolling.
Both first-launch Tool setup captures show legible options, scrollable pack selection and footer actions.
limitations: Hosted Windows Server 2022 at 96 DPI only; this is not representative-PC, high-DPI, multi-monitor or physical-trackpad acceptance.
Reference-management and initial Tool setup BMPs use PrintWindow; they establish window layout, not that the complete window was unoccluded on the physical desktop.
The legacy scroll gate explicitly calls MoveWindow(main,0,0,1040,680,True). Its cropped panel captures are not evidence for initial main-window bounds or whole-window screen fit.

Scroll reference images use screen BitBlt after a requested clean redraw. This visual review does not itself establish absence of transient flashes; finite temporal sampling is recorded separately by the native scroll gate.
No application or validation source was modified during this visual review.
